Lessons.Title: Multiples of 10,000 and 100,000
ExplanationParagraphs:
Learning goal: You will reason about the position of numbers relative to your multiples of 1,000, 10,000, and 100,000.
Prior to this point, you have learned to compare and order large numbers. You have also read, written, and decomposed numbers in terms of place value. In this lesson, you look at the relationship between multi-digit numbers and multiples of 1,000, 10,000, and 100,000.
Core relationship: Multiples of 10,000 and 100,000 on a number line. Use neighboring multiples of the stated unit to bracket a number.

Local publisher 2021 source lesson activities: Warm-up:  Choral Count: Multiples of 1,000, 10,000, and 100,000	 (10 minutes); Activity 1:  On Which Line Do They Belong?	 (20 minutes); Activity 2:  Closer to Some Multiple 	 (15 minutes); Cool-down:  Near 627,800	 (5 minutes)
Source-aligned Edulytics model: How far below 70,000 is 68,000?
First-party Cool-down (not gated original): Between which two consecutive multiples of 100,000 does 235,000 lie?
Original visual/physical and peer-explanation activities still require teacher review.
